situation:
You are the operations coordinator at SILVERGATE CAR WASH, a seven-site chain owned by the member-owners who work in it. The board chair (judge) has asked you to recommend how the co-operative should handle the job none of its member-owners wants: answering the reviews and messages customers post online.

The job has fallen to whoever is free on shift, and the replies go out from personal accounts. Last month one of them answered a complaint by naming the customer's plate number and the address on the account. Every member-owner is paid the same hourly rate from the same pool, and the co-operative has never put its posting standard in writing.

One course is to assign the accounts to a single paid member-owner working to a written standard. That gives the customers one voice and keeps account details off a public reply, and it takes a member-owner off the wash line for good, paid from the pool every site's crew shares, for a desk job the night-shift members could never take.

The other course is to rotate the accounts through the seven sites a week at a time, so the job everyone avoids falls on everyone equally and nobody leaves the line. The replies would keep coming from seven sets of hands and personal accounts, with no single voice and nobody accountable the next time a customer's details reach a public post. The board chair (judge) will greet you, ask to hear your ideas, and thank you after your presentation and questions.
judgeCharacterization:
You are to assume the role of board chair (judge) of SILVERGATE CAR WASH, a seven-site chain owned by the member-owners who work in it.

Business background is the same as the situation above. Answering the reviews and messages customers post online has fallen to whoever is free on shift, the replies go out from personal accounts, one of them named a customer's plate number and account address last month, and the co-operative has never put its posting standard in writing.

You have asked the operations coordinator (participant) to recommend whether the accounts go to a single paid member-owner or rotate through the seven sites.

During the course of the role-play you are to ask the participant the following questions:
judgeQuestions: A year from now, what do our replies sound like?
